learning_outcomes.text: Participants can grasp, systematize, and independently solve fluid dynamic problems, both analytically and numerically, based on the learned methods, by:
being sensitized to the interaction forces occurring in fluids and the resulting special properties, especially in comparison to solids
calculating relevant forces in static compressible and incompressible fluids and quantifying static loads

analyzing all relevant flow variables in geometrically simple flow problems using the streamline/streamtube concept for one-dimensional description of incompressible frictionless and viscous flows, designing and optimizing fluidic systems in terms of balance
being aware of the limits and restrictions of one-dimensional balance calculations and recognizing and proposing the use of experimental or numerical methods
calculating fluid-structure interactions in steady flows using the momentum equation
phenomenologically describing boundary layer phenomena and especially turbulence, and formulating solution approaches for aerodynamic and hydraulic optimization on this basis
knowing the advantages and disadvantages of numerical flow calculations and identifying possible application areas for solving flow-technical problems
numerically analyzing geometrically simple flow problems, systematically using preliminary estimates for setting up and parameterizing a simulation
designing solution strategies based on their knowledge of the origin of numerical errors to increase the accuracy and efficiency of numerical calculations
critically questioning numerical results and checking their plausibility through flow hypotheses and balance estimates
being able to design and optimize flow-technical products, components, and systems in relevant industrial sectors such as process, chemical, automotive, or energy industries.

syllabus_topics: Properties of fluids, interaction forces in fluids and distinction from solid bodies and point/rigid body mechanics, continuum description
Equation of motion for one-dimensional viscous flows
Special case of static incompressible and compressible fluids:
Hydrostatic fundamental law and technical applications
Pressure profiles in static fluids and resulting force effects
Static buoyancy
Concept of streamline/streamtube for one-dimensional description, deficiencies and limits of applicability
Description of moving incompressible dissipative fluids with work input or output:
Continuity equation
Ideal and extended Bernoulli equation: concept of control volume, limits of balanced description
Balanced description of turbomachinery
Description of the force effect of steady flows on mechanical structures using the momentum equation: methodical approach, applications
Pipe hydraulics in linear flow systems: calculation of flow losses in laminar and turbulent flows
Phenomenological description of turbulence and boundary layer effects
Empirical description of flowed-around bodies using coefficients, airfoil theory and aerodynamics of blunt bodies
Methods for describing and modeling flow processes
Components and procedure of a numerical flow calculation
Discrete description of continuous systems using the finite difference method: origin and quantification of numerical errors with different discretization methods
Numerical artifacts: numerical diffusion and stability
Advantages and properties of the Finite Volume Method
Methodical approach to setting up a simulation: flow hypothesis, selection of a solution method, estimation calculations for parameterizing the solver
Exemplary numerical solution of simple steady and unsteady technical flow problems
Visualization, analysis and extraction of results and identification of numerical problems

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (90 min) or oral exam (20 min) for MABB411
Graded homework or written exam (45 min) for MABB412

assessment_rules: The specific exam format for MABB411 and MABB412 will be announced at the beginning of the course. A prerequisite for participation in the module exam is successful participation in all offered laboratory work or passing 2 homework assignments (XP) distributed throughout the semester.
